summary: The real-time desk lead writes a fresh free-form email to the shift traders almost every day. Each one gives that day's long or short position (hub, hours, MW, price, book) and often restates a standing rule about Enpower, CAPS, the service sheet, losses or lending, and some of these get resent or corrected. Two fixes would make the emails predictable and stop the repeats: a fixed position notice template and one standing real-time procedures checklist that the notices link to. Together they are worth about $114 a month ($1,368 a year) in the lead's handling time, and they lower the risk of deals being booked wrong.

current_workflow.step: Desk lead (Bill Williams) writes a free-form email to the shift group or shift.portland@enron.com giving the day's length or short: hub (NP-15/SP-15), hours (HE 7-22), MW, price, and the book (ST-WBOM, ST-CALI). The order and wording change from day to day.

Shift traders read the email and book the deals under the named book in Enpower. They check the position against CAPS and record ST-CALI sales or length in the service sheet beneath the desk's own activity.

For one-off structures (APS losses, El Paso lending, PGE John Day to Malin transmission), the lead spells out the Enpower entries deal by deal: which deal number to reuse or price, which leg is priced at zero, and the annuity to ST-NW. Scheduling (Lisa) or deal entry (Kate) may already have made the tag or the Enpower deals.
current_workflow.who: real-time desk lead, scheduling, deal entry

current_workflow.step: Standing procedures go out as separate ad hoc emails mixed in with daily positions: hourly BPA checkout for Frontier and GCPUD with initials on the service sheet, CAISO price cap and wheeling fees, OASIS transmission paths, and using the Enpower swap function instead of annuities.
When instructions are missed or change, the lead sends follow-ups and resends: schedule changes must be called in, copy the lead on EES sheets and cut notes, updated APX buys.

stall_points.description: Standing rules sit inside individual emails, not in one place the shift can look up, so the lead has to re-send and remind.
stall_points.quote: These schedule changes must be called in.  Just a reminder.

stall_points.description: A procedure already circulated by another trader is resent in full because no shared reference exists.
stall_points.quote: Ryan sent this email out once already, here it is again.

stall_points.description: Distribution rules for EES sheets and cut notes are not followed, so the lead sends a correction.
stall_points.quote: I should be copied on the EES sheets, and any cut notes to volume managament, the services desk, or other traders.

stall_points.description: Position updates arrive in pieces in follow-up emails, so traders have to piece the current position together from several messages.
stall_points.quote: We have also bought HE 21 and HE 22 from the APX.

stall_points.description: Deal-entry rules that are explained only in passing lead to booking errors and long disputes afterward.
stall_points.quote: Swaps have caused disputes that have dragged on for months in the past, so call me with any questions.

stall_points.description: Where the service sheet should record things changes by email, and every trader has to remember the change.
stall_points.quote: Going forward, please put all the ST-CALI sales or length in the service sheet beneath our activity.

solution.approach: Two artifacts replace free-form writing. The first is a fixed position notice template that the desk lead fills in each afternoon for the next flow day. It has one row per position with fields for date, long/short, hub (NP-15/SP-15), hours (HE range), MW, price, book (ST-WBOM, ST-CALI, ST-Whourly) and the Enpower deal number(s) if already made. It also has a line saying where the entry goes (CAPS line, service sheet section) and a 'special handling' line that points to a numbered checklist item, not a re-explanation. The second is a standing Real-Time Shift Procedures checklist kept as a single document with numbered items. Items cover booking position deals under the named book in Enpower and matching CAPS, logging ST-CALI activity beneath desk activity on the service sheet, hourly BPA checkout for Frontier and GCPUD with initials, calling in schedule changes, copying the lead on EES sheets and cut notes, losses deals (buy from EPE, sale to APS at zero), PGE John Day to Malin on the standing deal, EPE lending, the Enpower swap function and CAISO wheeling fee components. When a rule changes, the lead edits the checklist item and the next notice carries a one-line 'Checklist updated: item N' instead of a full new email. Corrections go out as a reissued notice with a version marker ('v2 replaces v1'), not as a loose follow-up.
solution.trigger: The desk lead's daily close of next-day positions (length or short in the BOM or ST-CALI books), plus any change to a standing real-time procedure.
inputs: next-day long/short positions by hub, hours, MW, price and book
Enpower deal numbers already created by deal entry or scheduling
changes to standing procedures (BPA checkout, losses, lending, swaps, CAISO fees)
outputs: daily position notice in a fixed format for the real-time shift traders
a numbered Real-Time Shift Procedures checklist the shift uses on every shift
a short 'checklist updated: item N' line when a rule changes
components: position notice email template (saved Outlook template or signature block) with fixed fields: date, long/short, hub, HE range, MW, price, book, Enpower deal #, CAPS line, special handling item #, version
Real-Time Shift Procedures checklist with numbered items and a change log
standing distribution list rule: notices go to shift.portland@enron.com with the lead and services desk copied

implementation_steps: Collect the standing rules already scattered across the lead's sent emails (BPA checkout, service sheet placement, ST-CALI logging, schedule-change call-ins, EES and cut note copies, losses to APS, PGE John Day to Malin, EPE lending, Enpower swap function, CAISO price cap and fee components, OASIS path notes) and write each as a numbered checklist item.
Have the shift traders review the draft checklist in the next real-time meeting, then publish it in one shared location next to the service sheet and preschedule sheet.
Build the position notice template with the fixed fields, with one row per position and a special-handling column that refers to checklist item numbers.
Starting on a set date, the desk lead sends every position notice from the template to shift.portland@enron.com, and sends corrections as reissued notices marked v2/v3.
Shift traders confirm each row against Enpower and CAPS and initial it on the service sheet, the same way they already initial the hourly BPA checkout.

Each time a rule changes, edit the checklist item, add a change-log line, and mention the item number in the next notice. After one month, check whether any separate reminder emails were still needed.
stays_manual: Deciding the position itself (how much length to carry, price, which book) stays with the desk lead because it is a trading judgment.
One-off structures not yet in the checklist (for example a new lending arrangement) still need a written explanation the first time. They become checklist items only once they recur.
Professional conduct issues and meeting announcements are not procedure and stay as normal email.
Traders still make the real-time calls (BPA checkout, EPE dispatchers, calling in schedule changes). The checklist reminds them but cannot make the call.
risks: The evidence comes from one mailbox (williams-w3), so how shift traders actually use CAPS and the service sheet is only seen through the lead's emails. Validate the checklist with the traders before rollout.
A stale checklist could mislead traders on price caps or deal numbers. Mitigate with a dated change log and by quoting the item number in each notice.
The savings are small (about $114 a month), so the case rests as much on fewer booking errors and swap disputes as on time saved. That benefit is not quantified in the evidence.
Traders may keep working from old emails. Mitigate by announcing that only template notices and the current checklist are authoritative.
success_metric: Count of separate reminder, correction or resend emails from the desk lead to the shift group per month (for example 'just a reminder', 'one more time', 'here it is again') after rollout compared with before, plus the share of position emails sent in the template format.
